title: 2013 AMC 12A Problem 23
statement: \(ABCD\) is a square of side length \(\sqrt{3} + 1.\) Point \(P\) is on \(\overline{AC}\) such that \(AP = \sqrt{2}.\) The square region bounded by \(ABCD\) is rotated \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise with center \(P,\) sweeping out a region whose area is \(\dfrac{1}{c}(a\pi + b),\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are positive integers and \(\gcd(a, b, c) = 1.\) What is \(a + b + c?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(A', B', C', D'\) be the images of the vertices under the rotation. The swept region decomposes into four circular sectors and four triangles.

Since \(AP = \sqrt{2}\) and \(PC = AC - AP = \sqrt{6},\) the sectors at \(A\) and \(C\) have areas \(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\tfrac{3\pi}{2}.\) If \(H\) is the midpoint of \(AA',\) then \(PH=AH=1\) and \(HB=\sqrt3,\) so \(\triangle BPH\) is a \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle and \(PB=2.\) Hence the two \(60^\circ\) sectors along \(BC\) each have area \(\frac{2\pi}{3}.\) The two triangles with altitude \(PH\) contribute \(\sqrt3-1,\) and the other congruent pair has altitude \(\sqrt3\) and contributes \(3-\sqrt3.\) Thus the four triangles contribute \(2.\)

The total area is \[ \begin{gathered} \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{3\pi}{2} + 2\cdot\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + 2 \\ = \dfrac{10\pi + 6}{3}, \end{gathered} \] so \(a + b + c = 10 + 6 + 3 = 19.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Track the images \(A', B', C', D';\) the swept region is four circular sectors plus four triangles
